benchmark: one-step Minecraft version bump on real open-source Fabric/Architectury mods
jdk: Temurin 21 (C:/Users/Jk101/tools/jdk-21). JDK 25 was tried first and every mod's Gradle 8.11-8.14 wrapper rejected it: "BUG! ... Unsupported class file major version 69" (log-jdk25-probe.txt).
method: git clone --depth 1 at a 1.21.x branch -> .\gradlew.bat build -x test --console=plain (baseline) -> edit only version pins (minecraft_version, yarn/mojang mappings, fabric_api_version, plus loader/loom/third-party pins only when resolution or tooling forced it) -> rebuild -> count javac errors. Builds ran 1-4 in parallel on one machine.
caveat: Wall seconds include Gradle startup and dependency/MC setup. Baselines were cold (fresh clone: Gradle distribution + full dependency graph); bumped builds reused warm caches, so bump seconds understate the extra work and baseline seconds include one-off downloads. Bump seconds still include the new Minecraft jar download + remap.

mods.notes: Needed 3 attempts but only 1 of them was compile-tooling: attempts 1 and 2 died on disk exhaustion ('There is not enough space on the disk') while several Loom builds shared the cache volume. A control run at the ORIGINAL Loom 1.10.5 + Gradle 8.12.1 also reached compileJava and produced the same 136 error lines, so no Loom/Gradle bump was required for 1.21.6.
